words.games.title: NHL Games
words.games.lede: Today's, tomorrow's and yesterday's NHL games: each team's chance of winning, where to watch, and the score as it happens.
words.games.note: The visiting team is on the left, and the channel or streaming service is on the right. The number beside each team is its place in the league standings today, also for earlier days. Choose a team to see its whole season.
words.games.odds_note: Percentages are each team's chance of winning, from this site's own ratings of results, opponents and home ice; they are not betting lines.
words.games.live_note: Live scores from ESPN, refreshed every {seconds} seconds.
words.standings.title: NHL Standings
words.standings.lede: The league's own standings, as of {date}.
words.standings.lede_goat: This site's own ranking of the 32 teams, from record, strength of schedule, expected-goal share and goal share, with a boost for a team on a hot streak.
words.standings.note: Two points for a win, one for a loss in overtime or a shootout. Teams level on points are separated the league's way: fewer games played, then regulation wins. Hold or hover over a column heading for what it means; choose a team to see its page.
words.standings.note_line: The line marks the playoff places: the top three in each division, and the two best of the rest in each conference as wild cards.
words.standings.note_goat: The same columns as the standings, in this site's order. League is the team's place in the standings; SOS ranks the 32 by how strong the teams they have played are (1 is the hardest); xG% is the team's share of the expected goals in its games and G% its share of the actual goals. Redone after every game.
words.standings.note_goat_how: Each team gets its place among the 32 on four things: record (30%), expected-goal share (30%), goal share (25%) and strength of schedule (15%). A team that has won {from} or more in a row is hot and gets a boost for each win in the streak. Expected goals add up how likely each shot was to go in, from where and how it was taken, so they say who has had the better chances whatever the bounces.
words.teams.title: NHL Team Stats
words.teams.lede: How each team scores, shoots, defends and plays special teams, per game, from official box scores.
words.teams.note: xGF and xGA are expected goals: how many goals the team's chances, and its opponents', were worth, from where and how each shot was taken. Rating is where this site's rating of results (the one behind the odds) places the team; SOS ranks the 32 by how strong their opponents have been. Choose a column heading to sort; hold or hover over a heading for what it means.
words.team.players_note: # is his rank by Impact per game among all regular skaters in the league (goalies are ranked among goalies); part-time players are greyed and not ranked. Choose a name for his card.
words.players.title: NHL Players
words.players.lede: Every regular in the NHL, ranked by Impact per game: the points he adds per game over an average player at his position.
words.players.note: Impact is a box-score rating: a goal is worth 0.75, a first assist 0.70, a second assist 0.55, a shot on goal 0.075, a blocked shot 0.05, a takeaway 0.03 (a giveaway costs the same), a minor penalty drawn 0.15 (one taken costs the same) and each goal of plus-minus 0.15. A player's total is compared with what an average forward or defenseman would have in the same ice time. It cannot see shot quality or who else was on the ice, and it does not adjust for the opponent. Early in the season a few games can move a player a long way.
words.players.note_goalies: A goalie's Impact is the goals he saved beyond what an average goalie would have on the same number of shots (at even strength, against the power play and shorthanded), at 0.75 a goal. Impact does not see shot quality; goals saved above expected, on his card, does. Early in the season a game or two can move a goalie a long way.
words.lines.title: NHL Line Combinations
words.lines.lede: Each team's forward lines, defense pairs, power-play and penalty-kill units and goalies, as they actually played in its last game. Choose a team.
words.lines.heading: Lines
words.lines.none: No lines yet: this team has not played a game with a shift chart this season.
words.lines.note: These are worked out from the league's shift charts, not announced by the team: the three forwards (and two defensemen) who spent the most five-on-five time together in the last game are a line, then the next among the rest. Lines are numbered by how much their players play: their ice time a game this season, power play and penalty kill included. So the first pair is the one on the ice most, even when its two also take shifts with others. Power-play and penalty-kill units are the groups out together most over the last {n} games. A line broken up during the game, an injury or a benching shows as it happened. Left and right sides go by each player's listed position and shooting hand, so a center playing wing may be shown in the middle. Choose a player for his card.
words.lines.on_title: This season at five-on-five with this group out: goals for and against, and their share of the expected goals
words.lines.stats_lede: What has happened this season at five-on-five while each line and pair was on the ice.
words.lines.stats_note: Every line and pair with at least 10 minutes together at five-on-five this season, the 15 with the most. GF and GA are goals for and against while they were out; xGF and xGA are expected goals, what the shots were worth; xG% is their share of those, so over 50% means they had the better of the chances. Shots% is their share of all shot attempts, blocked ones included. A shot counts for the five skaters on the ice in the second before it. A few minutes together say little: these settle down over a season. Select a column heading to sort by it.
words.game.note: During a game the score comes from ESPN and updates every 15 seconds; player stats come from the NHL's box score and are refreshed about every 5 minutes. A dark edge marks the defensemen.
words.footer.about: Game times are shown in your own time zone. Schedules, scores, standings, channels and box scores come from the NHL's public feed, and scores of games in progress from ESPN's. Channels can change, so check before you tune in; streaming services need their own subscription. Chances of winning, the GOAT ranking and player ratings are worked out by this site. Team logos and player photos belong to the NHL and its teams and are shown from the league's own site. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the NHL or any team.
words.odds.title: NHL Playoff Odds
words.odds.lede: Each team's chance of making the playoffs, reaching each round and winning the Stanley Cup, from playing out the rest of the season {sims} times.
words.odds.none: The odds have not been worked out yet. They will be here after the next update.
words.odds.note: These are this site's own estimate, not a sportsbook's line. Every coming game is decided by the chance of winning shown on the Games page; the standings, the wild cards and the bracket follow the league's rules, and each series is best of seven. Because nobody knows exactly how good a team is, least of all early in the season, each team's rating is moved up or down by a random amount every time the season is played out. Points is the average finish. Week is how far the chance of the playoffs has moved in seven days. Select a column heading to sort by it.
words.odds.tested: Tested on {seasons}, at seven points in each season: of the teams given {high_range} to make the playoffs, {high} did; of those given {top_range}, {top}; of those given {low_range}, {low}.
